newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: San Miguel sees profit boost from merger.
newsitem.headline: San Miguel sees profit boost from merger.

text.p: Beverage maker San Miguel Corp said on Thursday it expects a proposed merger of its soft drinks interests with Coca-Cola Co's Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd of Australia to add to profits in 1997 and in the future.
In a statement, the maker of beer and other products said, "San Miguel expects the transaction will enhance net income in 1997 and beyond." It did not offer specific projections.

San Miguel officials are scheduled to hold a special news briefing in Manila later on Thursday at 2 p.m. local time (0600 GMT). Its B stock was down 50 centavos at 91 pesos, and its A shares were unchanged at 55 pesos late on Thursday.
Earlier on Thursday, Coca-Cola Amatil announced that San Miguel would become its second largest shareholder through the merger, which would give the Philippine company a 25 percent stake.
Coca-Cola Co is still the biggest stockholder with 33 percent ownership.
Under the deal, Coca-Cola Amatil would issue 293 million shares worth about $2.7 billion, San Miguel said.
The merger of San Miguel's unit Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc with Coca-Cola Amatil would create the biggest Coca-Cola bottling group outside the United States.
Three representatives from San Miguel will be invited to join the board of Coca-Cola Amatil, the statement said.
